query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Patient; SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT ID) FROM Patient;
result: 1238 rows and 1238 distinct IDs.
validation_method: row count and key uniqueness check

query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Examination; SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT ID) FROM Examination; SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT ID FROM Examination GROUP BY ID HAVING COUNT(*) > 1);
result: 806 rows, 763 distinct patient IDs, 8 IDs with more than one examination row.

query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Laboratory; SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT ID) FROM Laboratory; SELECT MAX(c) FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) c FROM Laboratory GROUP BY ID);
result: 13908 rows, 302 distinct patient IDs, maximum 226 rows for a single patient, average about 46 rows per patient.

query: SELECT MIN(ID), MAX(ID), COUNT(DISTINCT ID) FROM Patient;
result: Minimum 2110, maximum 5845877, 1238 distinct values. IDs are sparse multi-digit integers.

query: SELECT SEX, COUNT(*) FROM Patient GROUP BY SEX;
result: F 1023, M 202, empty string 13.

query: SELECT MIN(Birthday), MAX(Birthday), SUM(Birthday IS NULL) FROM Patient;
result: Range 1912-08-28 to 2007-05-28 with 1 NULL birthday.

query: PRAGMA table_info(Patient) followed by inspection of the Birthday column; SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Patient WHERE Birthday IS NOT NULL;
result: No age column exists in Patient; the only temporal source for age is Birthday, so age has to be derived by comparing Birthday with a reference date.

query: SELECT Admission, COUNT(*) FROM Patient GROUP BY Admission;
result: '+' 488, '-' 713, '+' with trailing character 3, empty string 34.

query: SELECT Diagnosis, COUNT(*) FROM Patient GROUP BY Diagnosis ORDER BY 2 DESC;
result: Many distinct free-text values. Most frequent single codes: SLE 195, SJS 160, RA 152, BEHCET 90, PSS 45; combinations such as 'SLE, SJS' 35, 'RA, SJS' 25, 'SLE, APS' 15 also occur. 244 rows contain a comma and 154 rows contain 'susp'.

query: SELECT Diagnosis, COUNT(*) FROM Examination GROUP BY Diagnosis ORDER BY 2 DESC;
result: 331 of 806 rows are NULL. Remaining values use the same vocabulary as Patient but spell Sjogren's syndrome as 'SjS' (41 rows) and show 'SLE' 95, 'RA' 29, 'APS' 10.

query: SELECT 'SJS'='SjS', 'SJS' LIKE '%SjS%', 'SJS' LIKE 'sjS'; SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Patient WHERE Diagnosis = 'SLE'; SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Patient WHERE Diagnosis = 'sle'; SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Patient WHERE Diagnosis LIKE 'sle';
result: Equality returns 0 while both substring comparisons return 1, confirming that equality is case sensitive and substring matching is case insensitive. 'SLE' equality matched 195 rows, 'sle' equality matched 0 rows, and the case-insensitive substring form matched 195 rows. Both Patient and Examination draw on the same code vocabulary, with 'SJS' used in Patient and 'SjS' in Examination.
validation_method: comparison-operator behaviour test on real values

query: SELECT Thrombosis, COUNT(*) FROM Examination GROUP BY Thrombosis;
result: 0: 726 rows, 1: 57 rows, 2: 18 rows, 3: 5 rows.

query: SELECT SUM(Symptoms IS NOT NULL), SUM(Thrombosis <> 0) FROM Examination; SELECT Thrombosis, COUNT(*), SUM(Symptoms IS NOT NULL) FROM Examination GROUP BY Thrombosis;
result: Symptoms is non-NULL for exactly 80 rows, identical to the 80 rows with Thrombosis <> 0. Grouped by grade, the non-NULL symptom count is 0 for grade 0 and equals the full row count for grades 1, 2 and 3.

query: SELECT MIN('Examination Date'), MAX('Examination Date'), SUM('Examination Date' IS NULL) FROM Examination;
result: Range 1989-04-18 to 1998-04-17 with 10 NULL dates.

query: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT Description), COUNT(*) FROM Patient WHERE Description IS NOT NULL AND Description <> ''; SELECT ID, SEX, Diagnosis FROM Patient WHERE Description = '1994-02-19'; SELECT ID, 'Examination Date', 'aCL IgM' FROM Examination WHERE ID IN (SELECT ID FROM Patient WHERE Description = '1994-02-19');
result: 97 distinct values across 1022 non-empty rows, so the value is shared by groups of patients. The date '1994-02-19' selects 24 patients including ID 283032 whose diagnosed condition is SLE and whose examination on 1993-11-12 carries aCL IgM 4.1, matching the workload statement that a patient diagnosed with SLE on 1994/2/19 had that examination result.
validation_method: targeted value lookup reproducing a workload statement

query: SELECT MIN('First Date'), MAX('First Date'), SUM('First Date' IS NULL OR 'First Date' = ''), SUM(Description < 'First Date') FROM Patient;
result: Range 1972-08-02 to 1998-08-28; 251 rows NULL or empty; 12 rows have a record date earlier than the first visit date.

query: SELECT MIN(Date), MAX(Date) FROM Laboratory; SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Laboratory WHERE Date = '0000-00-00';
result: Range 1981-01-27 to 1999-03-04 with 0 rows carrying the zero-date placeholder.

query: SELECT ANA, COUNT(*) FROM Examination GROUP BY ANA ORDER BY 2 DESC;
SELECT 'ANA Pattern', COUNT(*) FROM Examination GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC;
result: S 252, P 178, 'P,S' 89, 'S,P' 11, 'D,P,S' 2, 'S,D' 2, lowercase 'p' 2, and 261 NULL rows, showing combined letter codes and case variation.

query: SELECT SUM('aCL IgG' IS NULL), SUM('aCL IgM' IS NULL), SUM('aCL IgA' IS NULL), MIN('aCL IgG'), MAX('aCL IgG'), MIN('aCL IgA'), MAX('aCL IgA'), MIN('aCL IgM'), MAX('aCL IgM') FROM Examination;
result: No NULL values in any of the three isotype columns. Ranges: aCL IgG 0.0 to 2150.3, aCL IgA 0 to 48547, aCL IgM 0.0 to 187122.0, with a large mass of values at or near 0.

query: SELECT SM, COUNT(*) FROM Laboratory GROUP BY SM ORDER BY 2 DESC;
result: Non-empty values: '0' 102 rows, 'negative' 20 rows, '1' 4 rows, '8' 1 row, '2' 1 row; the remaining 13780 rows are NULL. Both '0' and 'negative' therefore express a negative result.

query: Grouped counts over CRP, RA, SSA, SSB, RNP, U-PRO in Laboratory.
result: CRP combines '-', '<0.3', '<0.2', '+', '2+' and plain numeric strings; RA combines '-', '+', '+-', '2+' and one stray '7-'; SSA and RNP mix '0', 'negative' and numeric titres up to 256; U-PRO uses '-', 'TR', '0' and small integers. The same conceptual class therefore appears in several spellings within one column.

query: SELECT MIN(UA), MAX(UA), SUM(UA > 8.0), SUM(UA > 6.5), COUNT(UA) FROM Laboratory;
result: Range 0.4 to 17.3 with 698 non-NULL values; 224 records exceed 8.0 and 698 exceed 6.5.

query: SELECT MIN(HCT), MAX(HCT), SUM(HCT >= 52), SUM(HCT < 10), COUNT(HCT) FROM Laboratory;
result: Range 3.0 to 56.0; 30 records are at or above 52 and 11 records are below 10, the latter being implausible as physiological hematocrit values.
validation_method: range, threshold count and outlier inspection

query: SELECT MIN(RBC), MAX(RBC), SUM(RBC < 3.5), COUNT(RBC) FROM Laboratory;
result: Range 0.4 to 6.6; 759 records are below 3.5.

query: SELECT MIN(LDH), MAX(LDH), SUM(LDH > 500), AVG(LDH) FROM Laboratory;
result: Range 25 to 67080 with mean 322.27; 1281 records exceed 500.

query: SELECT MIN(PT), MAX(PT), SUM(PT >= 14), AVG(PT), COUNT(PT) FROM Laboratory;
result: Range 10.1 to 27.0 with mean 13.27; 183 of the non-NULL records are at or above 14.

query: SELECT MIN(IGA), MAX(IGA), SUM(IGA > 80 AND IGA < 500), COUNT(IGA) FROM Laboratory;
result: Range 1 to 1765; 2204 of 2680 non-NULL records fall inside the open interval 80 to 500.

query: SELECT AVG('T-CHO'), COUNT('T-CHO') FROM Laboratory;
result: Mean 203.06 across the stored non-NULL values; the column holds one integer value per test date rather than a change measure.

query: PRAGMA table_info(Laboratory); SELECT SUM(SM IS NULL), SUM(CRP IS NULL), SUM(HCT IS NULL) FROM Laboratory;
result: The table has 47 analyte columns and a composite primary key (ID, Date). Missing measurements are common: SM is NULL in 13780 of 13908 rows and different analytes are NULL on different rows, confirming that a row represents a test event rather than a complete panel.
validation_method: schema inspection and per-column NULL counts

query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Examination e JOIN Patient p ON e.ID = p.ID; SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Examination e LEFT JOIN Patient p ON e.ID = p.ID WHERE p.ID IS NULL; SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Laboratory l LEFT JOIN Patient p ON l.ID = p.ID WHERE p.ID IS NULL;
result: Examination joins to Patient on only 70 of 806 rows (69 distinct patients); 736 examination rows have no matching patient. Laboratory has 0 unmatched rows out of 13908. The unmatched examination ID range reaches 9334040 against a maximum Patient ID of 5845877.
validation_method: join coverage measurement in both directions

query: SELECT name, sql FROM sqlite_master WHERE type = 'table';
result: The schema contains only the three base tables Patient, Examination and Laboratory with raw attribute and measurement columns. No column stores a percentage, ratio, rate or age.
